question: A trading desk stakeholder wants Claude to report the current live stock price directly from its own knowledge, without connecting any external data source. How should this limitation be explained?
options: A) Explain that real-time data requests always trigger a permission error and there is no supported way, such as a webhook, to add live data access.
B) Explain that stock prices are static values set at the daily close, so any past training data would reflect the official price and remain accurate today.
C) Explain that Claude has no access to live, real-time data on its own, so a tool like web search must be connected to fetch current prices.
D) Explain that Claude continuously streams live market data through a direct internal feed from major exchanges, so no external tool integration is ever required.
correct_answers: C) Explain that Claude has no access to live, real-time data on its own, so a tool like web search must be connected to fetch current prices.
explanations: Incorrect. Real-time data requests do not always trigger a permission error; Claude supports tool integrations like web search or webhooks to access live data. There are supported methods to add live data access.

Incorrect. Stock prices are not static values set at the daily close; they change constantly during trading hours. Past training data reflects historical prices and would be outdated, not accurate today.

Correct. Claude has no built-in ability to access live, real-time data on its own; its knowledge is static, drawn from training data. To retrieve current stock prices, an external tool such as web search must be connected and invoked.

Incorrect. Claude does not continuously stream live market data internally; it has no direct feed from major exchanges. Real-time information requires integration with an external data source or tool.
